problemStatement.formal:
Let $r\geq 2$ and let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a set of maximal size such that there are at most $r$ solutions to $n=a+b$ with $a\leq b$ for any $n$. (That is, $A$ is a $B_2[r]$ set.)

Similarly, let $B\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a set of maximal size such that there are at most $r$ solutions to $n=a-b$ for any $n$.

If $\lvert A\rvert\sim c_rN^{1/2}$ as $N\to \infty$ and $\lvert B\rvert \sim c_r'N^{1/2}$ as $N\to \infty$ then is it true that $c_r\neq c_r'$ for $r\geq 2$? Is it true that $c_r'<c_r$?



According to Erd\H{o}s, first formulated in conversation with Berend, and later independently reformulated with Freud.

It is true that $c_1=c_1'$, and the classical bound on the size of Sidon sets (see [30]) implies $c_1=c_1'=1$.
problemStatement.plain: Let $r\geq 2$ and let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a set of maximal size such that there are at most $r$ solutions to $n=a+b$ with $a\leq b$ for any $n$. (That is, $A$ is a $B_2[r]$ set.)
whyMatters: Sidon sets and their B₂[r] generalizations are central objects in additive combinatorics, with deep connections to Singer difference sets, finite projective planes, and number-theoretic counting problems
The conjectured asymmetry between sums and differences (cᵣ vs c'ᵣ) tests our understanding of why r = 1 is special — the unordered/ordered structure shift only manifests for multiple representations
Quantitative results (Cilleruelo-Ruzsa-Trujillo 2002, Ruzsa) give Θ-bounds but lack the precision needed to separate cᵣ from c'ᵣ — closing this gap likely requires new methods

proven: Sidon case (r = 1): c₁ = c'₁ = 1 — Erdős-Turán upper bound + Singer lower bound, classical
B₂[r] sets in {1,...,N} have size Θ(√(rN)) — Cilleruelo, Ruzsa, Trujillo (2002): |A| ≤ √(rN) + O(r^{1/2}N^{1/4})
Ruzsa: cᵣ ~ √r with constructions achieving cᵣ ≥ √r - o(1)
open: Main conjecture: c'ᵣ < cᵣ for r ≥ 2 (Erdős, with Berend and Freud, [Er92c])
Weaker: cᵣ ≠ c'ᵣ for some r ≥ 2
Even existence of the limiting constants cᵣ and c'ᵣ for r ≥ 2 is nontrivial — current results give Θ-bounds, not asymptotic equalities
